forces.title: Hydro portfolios maintain value in dynamic energy markets
forces.description: In the evolving power and gas trading landscape, traditional asset-backed trading is under pressure, but hydro portfolios are noted for their ability to retain value. This resilience stems from the flexibility hydro assets offer, allowing traders to adapt to shifting forward prices. This inherent characteristic positions hydropower as a stable and valuable component for traders navigating increasing market volatility and shorter trading windows, providing a consistent hedge against market fluctuations. This makes hydro attractive in a context where many traditional models are facing challenges, underscoring its role in ensuring market stability and profitability for asset-backed trading firms in the medium term.
forces.source_title: Power, Gas, and LNG Trading: Racing to Compete in the Coming Decade

forces.title: Hybrid PPAs integrate hydro for enhanced renewable flexibility
forces.description: The growth in origination and structuring business models within energy trading is shifting towards products that price in flexibility, such as structured power purchase agreements (PPAs). Hybrid PPAs, which combine complementary renewable sources like wind and hydro, are emerging as a key development. This trend indicates that hydropower's dispatchability and storage capabilities are being strategically leveraged to create more stable and attractive renewable energy products. This integration enhances the value proposition of variable sources like wind, offering a significant opportunity for hydropower in facilitating the overall transition to a flexible, renewable-dominated energy system over the medium term.
